title: Uniform perimeter improvement of planar radial cluster stars with more than three rays for strictly convex anisotropic densities smooth in direction
source_title: On the Steiner property for planar minimizing clusters. The anisotropic case
author: Valentina Franceschi; Aldo Pratelli; Giorgio Stefani
difficulty_reason: Euclidean120-degree junction arguments do not establish a competitor for a nonsymmetric anisotropic perimeter, whose exterior and interior interfaces have different costs. The source constructs competitors in all white/colored configurations and uses first-order tangent estimates to rule out the nondegenerate cases, then builds a separate three-segment competitor for the degenerate four-sector case. The small-angle reduction and compactness turn these strict improvements into a uniform positive gain, leaving a complete geometric construction beyond routine convexity terminology.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Independent substantial Proposition2.3, the anisotropic90degree property: strictly positive positively homogeneous density with strictly convex unit ball and C1 direction dependence, finite radial star inside unit disk with more than three boundary radii. A competitor equal outside the disk lowers the specified cluster perimeter by delta(h)>0. The competitor is not asserted to preserve chamber volumes, so do not reinterpret it as a full isoperimetric regularity theorem. Read exactstatement14 and all consecutive five-step core14–20; precise asymmetric perimeter convention3–4/8–9 and clockwise normal/tangent conversion13 retained. C1 is the directional hypothesis on S1 used in Definitions1.1/TheoremA, despite the shorthand ambient C1 expression at14 for its homogeneous extension. No uniform roundedness or spatial Dini condition is imposed for this independent star theorem. The uniformly round nonsmooth quadruple-junction examples3.1/3.2 are held: existence of the global density forcing the stated minimizer boundary data is explicitly omitted46. No new global smoothing/minimizer argument supplied. Main Steiner regularity is not selected or claimed fully read. historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The author handles genuinely asymmetric perimeter costs at exterior and interior interfaces through five distinct local competitor constructions. First-order supporting-normal estimates rule out ordinary multiple rays, while a coupled two-ray replacement deals with the exceptional four-ray configuration; compactness upgrades pointwise improvements to a uniform gain. This anisotropic cluster surgery is above qualifying-exam convex geometry.
